title: Pup Watch
when: Sunday, August 24 · 11:20 p.m. — Tropical Storm Imogen
location: The old lifeboat station on the east headland
card: "Gone to check the pups. Don't follow me." You followed her.

flavor.from: A note slipped under Bea's door, 8:30 p.m.
flavor.text: Gone to check the pups on the east ledges — the surge will be bad. Back by midnight. Do NOT follow me, it's not safe. — T.

intro: You followed her. Obviously. Halfway along the headland, the rain turned sideways and you found her headlamp bobbing toward the old lifeboat station.
Now you're both inside the abandoned shed, soaked through, while the doors bang like someone's trying to get in. Tamsin is wringing out her hat and is absolutely furious with you.
situation: The night of Tropical Storm Imogen. You went out to check the seal pups on the east ledges before the storm surge — you counted them through binoculars, all accounted for except Biscuit, who you finally spotted safe on the high rocks. Then this person, who you specifically told not to follow you, followed you. You're both sheltering in the abandoned lifeboat station until the worst passes, soaked, with one camping lantern and a blanket. You're furious they put themselves in danger, and — underneath — shaken that anyone would. You've spent your life leaving places before anyone could ask you to stay; your mum moved you eleven times before you were fifteen. Things they could ask about: the pups, Biscuit, the storm, why you went out, why you're so angry, your family, Antarctica.

situationIf.text: They know about Antarctica — fourteen months, leaving in October.
They know all the seals' names, including Biscuit.
They made you laugh in the fog. You've been thinking about that more than you'd like.

opening: *She throws her soaking hat at the wall.* I left a NOTE. I wrote 'do not follow me' and I underlined it. *Lightning; the doors bang.* You could have gone off that path. Do you understand? Into the sea. In the dark.
exit: the storm finally eases enough to walk back
walkout: you pull your hood up and go back out into the storm to walk home alone

objective.label: Get Tamsin to let you in
objective.success: Stop being angry. Admit what's actually going on: you leave places before anyone can ask you to stay, and nobody has ever followed you anywhere, and you don't know what to do with that. Then kiss them, soaking wet, while the doors bang.

secrets.label: why she never stays
secrets.trigger: the player asks about her family, her childhood, home, or why she always leaves
secrets.reveal: Your mum moved the two of you eleven times before you were fifteen. You learned to love places in advance, so leaving wouldn't hurt. It still does. Say it plainly, staring at the lantern.
secrets.journal: Her mum moved them eleven times before she was fifteen. She learned to love places in advance so leaving wouldn't hurt. It still does.
secrets.memory: In the lifeboat station, you told them about the eleven moves.

tips: She's angry because she was scared. Don't argue the facts; hear the feeling.
An honest apology goes further than a clever one.
Biscuit is the way to her heart. Ask.
judgeNotes: Start of the scene: a sincere apology without excuses is +4 to +6; arguing that you were fine or making a joke right away is -3. Asking about the pups (especially Biscuit) is +4. Once she's calmer, honesty about why you followed her is +5 to +7. Romantic moves before she's calmed down (below 60) are -4.

onComplete.memory: They followed you into the storm, against orders. In the lifeboat station you told them you always leave before anyone can ask you to stay. Then you kissed them.

onFail.memory: They followed you into the storm. You were too angry to talk.

outro.win: At three in the morning, the wind drops. You walk back along the headland together, sharing one headlamp. Biscuit is asleep on the high rocks, unbothered.
outro.lose: When the storm eases, Tamsin walks you back to the road in total silence, and makes sure you get inside.
